documents.content:
Release approval

A production deployment requires one approval from the service owner and one from the on-call engineer. The author of the change cannot supply both approvals. Emergency releases use the same two-person rule.

Rollback policy

Rollback starts when the error rate remains above five percent for ten minutes or when checkout availability falls below 99 percent. The release operator restores the last verified artifact and records the incident number.

Canary rollout

The first stage receives five percent of traffic for fifteen minutes. Promotion requires stable latency, error rate and saturation. A failed canary is stopped automatically and never advances to the regional stage.

Database changes

Destructive schema changes require an expand-and-contract migration. Backfills run with a fixed rate limit and a resumable cursor. Application rollback must remain possible until the old columns are no longer read.

Incident severity

Severity one means complete customer outage or confirmed data loss. Severity two covers major degradation without data loss. Lower severity events stay in the team queue and do not page the executive responder.

Alert routing

Checkout alerts page the commerce on-call rotation. Data pipeline alerts go to analytics operations. Security alerts are sent to the security response rotation; they are not routed through the general help desk.

Logging privacy

Logs may contain request identifiers and coarse timing but must exclude passwords, authentication tokens, payment card numbers and full message bodies. Sensitive fields are removed before export to the central collector.

Retention periods

Application logs are retained for thirty days. Deployment audit events are retained for one year. Temporary debug captures expire after twenty-four hours and require an incident reference when enabled.

Service objectives

The checkout API targets 99.9 percent monthly availability and a 400 millisecond p95 latency. These are internal objectives, not contractual customer guarantees. Error-budget exhaustion pauses feature releases.

Dependency failure

Calls to the tax provider time out after two seconds and may retry once with jitter. If failures continue, checkout returns a temporary unavailable response; it must not silently use a zero tax value.

Feature flags

Every temporary flag has an owner and expiry date. Permission changes and payment behavior cannot be enabled for all users without a staged rollout. Expired flags are removed rather than permanently disabled.

Postmortem process

Severity one and two incidents require a blameless review within five business days. The document includes a timeline, customer impact, contributing conditions and assigned corrective actions with due dates.
